subject: sauna
title: What If You Stayed in a Sauna Too Long?

scenes.text: What if you stayed in a sauna far too long? The hot air isn't the real danger.
A Finnish sauna runs about 80 to 100 degrees Celsius, but the air is dry, so your sweat can cool you.
Throw water on the stones, and the humidity jumps. Now the heat hits your skin much harder.
Stay too long, and your core passes 40 degrees. That's heat stroke: confusion, then collapse.
In 2010, the World Sauna Championship ran at 110 degrees, with water thrown on the stones.
After about six minutes, both finalists collapsed. One died. The contest was never held again.

description:
Finnish saunas usually run at 80-100 °C with low humidity (10-20%); throwing water on the stones briefly raises temperature and humidity. Heat stroke typically means a core temperature above 40 °C.
At the 2010 World Sauna Championships in Heinola, Finland, held at 110 °C, both finalists collapsed after about six minutes; one died and the event was never held again.
